mainTopic: נדרי זרוזין: who taught the משנה of the four vows, and do sharply worded bargaining vows count as real vows?
overview: This amud opens with the last line of the משנה about נדרי זרוזין, vows made while bargaining: both sides really want to settle at three דינרים, so their extreme vows do not bind. The גמרא asks who taught this משנה. רבי אבא בר ממל quotes רבי יהודה נשיאה, who said it follows רבי יהודה, because רבי יהודה holds that נזירות takes effect only with clear, certain intent (הפלאה). רבא answers that even the רבנן can agree, because the משנה says 'both want', in the present tense, so they never meant the vows at all. רבינא then asks רב אשי about a sharper case: one vows on 'more than a סלע' and the other on 'less than a שקל'. Is that a real vow, or still just pressure? רב אשי answers from a משנה where a guest refusing a meal vowed not to taste 'a drop of cold water', yet he may still drink. That shows people simply talk this way, and the same is true of the bargainers. The amud ends as רבינא begins to reply, and his reply continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the משנה: both sides really want three דינרים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה closes the case of bargaining vows: both sides actually want to settle at three דינרים, so the vows were only pressure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both of them want to settle at three דינרים.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the משנה about נדרי זרוזין. It explains why the extreme vows the buyer and seller made do not bind them: both really want the middle price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller vowed not to go below a סלע, and the buyer vowed not to go above a שקל. The משנה says these were never real commitments. Both were really aiming for three דינרים, so the vows were just bargaining pressure.

keyTerms.meaning: Both of them (the buyer and the seller)
They want (present tense). The גמרא will build an argument on this exact word.
Dinars, silver coins. Three דינרים is the middle price between the two vows.
Vows of pressure. Vows made only to push the other side in a deal.

steps.whyThisMatters: The present-tense word רוֹצִין becomes the key to רבא's answer in step 3.

phrases.english: Both of them want [to settle] at three dinars.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the משנה that began in the previous section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In bargaining vows, both sides really want the middle price, so the extreme vows are not binding.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יהודה: נזירות needs clear intent
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל reminds רבי אמי of his teaching in the name of רבי יהודה נשיאה: the משנה of four vows follows רבי יהודה, who says in the name of רבי טרפון that a vow without clear, certain intent does not take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא quotes the משנה: 'The Sages released four vows.' רבי אבא בר ממל said to רבי אמי: You told us in the name of רבי יהודה נשיאה: Who taught the משנה of the four vows? It is רבי יהודה. He said in the name of רבי טרפון that neither of them becomes a נזיר, because נזירות only takes effect with clear, certain intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking whose opinion the משנה follows. The answer given is רבי יהודה, who holds that a vow needs clear, definite intent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה ruled that when two people bet and each vows to be a נזיר, neither becomes one, because נזירות requires הפלאה, clear and certain intent. In the same way, a bargaining vow lacks real intent, so it is void. The suggestion is that the רבנן, who argue with רבי יהודה, might hold such vows binding.

keyTerms.meaning: They released, meaning they declared the vow not binding
Who taught? The גמרא's way of asking whose opinion a teaching follows
A person who vowed to be a nazirite
The state of being a נזיר
Clear, explicit, certain intent when making a vow

steps.confusionAlert: The quote about the נזיר comes from a different case, two people making a bet. It is brought only to show that רבי יהודה requires clear intent for a vow. The משנה here is about buying and selling.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
"The Sages released four vows," etc.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל לְרַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Memel said to Rabbi Ami:

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרְתְּ לַן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה:
phrases.english: You told us in the name of Rabbi Yehuda Nesia:
Who taught [the mishna of] the four vows?
It is Rabbi Yehuda,
who said in the name of Rabbi Tarfon:
Actually, neither one of them is a nazirite,
phrases.notes: "Them" means two people who made a bet, each vowing to be a נזיר if he turned out wrong.

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא נִיתְּנָה נְזִירוּת אֶלָּא לְהַפְלָאָה.
phrases.english: because nazirite status was given only with clear, explicit intent.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תְּנָא אַרְבָּעָה נְדָרִים — רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's discussion of the משנה by identifying which תנא it follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה follows רבי יהודה, who says a vow without clear, certain intent (הפלאה) does not take effect.

steps.title: Even the רבנן agree: the משנה says 'want', not 'wanted'
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה can follow the רבנן too, because it says 'both want' in the present tense. That shows they never really meant the vows at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You can even say the משנה follows the רבנן. Does it say 'both of them wanted'? It says 'both of them want.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on the claim that only רבי יהודה could hold this משנה. He shows the רבנן can agree as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה said 'they wanted' (past tense), it could sound like they changed their minds after making a real vow. Then only רבי יהודה's rule about unclear intent would save them. But 'they want' (present tense) means both were happy with three דינרים from the very start, so there was never a real vow. Even the רבנן agree that such a vow does not bind.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say. Used to show a teaching fits another opinion too
The Sages, the majority who argue with רבי יהודה
Does it teach...? Used to point at the exact wording of a source
They wanted (past tense)

steps.whatToRemember: רבא reads a lot into one word: 'want' (now) rather than 'wanted' (later). That shows there was never real intent to vow, so even the רבנן agree.

phrases.english: Rava said:
You can even say [it follows] the Rabbis,
Does it teach "both of them wanted"?
It teaches "both of them want."
phrases.notes: Present tense: they wanted three דינרים the whole time, even while they were making the vows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the need to say the משנה follows only רבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the משנה must follow רבי יהודה alone, without arguing with רבי יהודה's rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That view missed the present-tense word רוֹצִין, which shows there was never real intent to vow, so even the רבנן would agree.

steps.title: A bigger gap: 'more than a סלע' versus 'less than a שקל'
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי about a case where the seller vows on 'more than a סלע' and the buyer on 'less than a שקל'. Is that a real vow, or still just pressure?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: If one said 'more than a סלע' and the other said 'less than a שקל', is it a real vow, or is it just pressure?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא asks a new question that stretches the משנה's case. The two sides now stand even farther apart than in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the two vowed on a סלע and a שקל, so the middle price of three fits naturally. Here each one goes beyond those amounts, which might show they are dead serious, making it a real vow. Or it might still just be tougher bargaining. רב אשי answers in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: More (Aramaic)
Less (Aramaic)
A coin worth four דינרים
A coin worth two דינרים (half a סלע)
A real, binding vow
Pressure, pushing the other side, not a real vow

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
If [the seller] said to him, "more than a sela,"
and the other one says, "less than a shekel,"
is it a vow, or is it pressure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who taught the משנה to how far its rule reaches in a more extreme bargaining case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a bargaining vow that goes beyond the משנה's amounts (more than a סלע, less than a שקל) count as a binding vow, or is it still just pressure?

steps.title: רב אשי quotes a similar משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers by quoting a משנה about someone who refused an invitation with a vow. He vowed even on a drop of cold water, but he may still enter the house and drink cold water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: We already learned this. If someone was pressing his friend to eat with him, and the friend said, 'Your house is קונם for me to enter,' or 'A drop of cold water is קונם for me to taste,' he may still enter the house and drink cold water. He only meant to refuse a real meal of eating and drinking.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers רבינא's question from Step 4 by bringing a משנה with a similar case. Here too, a person used very sharp wording in a vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the guest's words sound very strict: not even a drop of water. Still, the משנה permits him to enter and drink, because all he meant was to refuse the meal. רב אשי will use this to show that sharp, exact-sounding words can still be just pressure.

keyTerms.meaning: Pressing or urging someone (here, to come eat)
A word used to make a vow, like saying 'forbidden as a קרבן'
Cold water

phrases.english: He said to him: We learned:
phrases.notes: רב אשי is answering רבינא's question from the last step.

phrases.english: If one was urging his friend
that he should eat with him,
and the friend said to him: 'Entering your house is konam for me,'
or: 'A drop of cold water is konam for me to taste'
phrases.notes: The word קונם from the first vow is understood here too, even though it isn't repeated.

phrases.english: he is permitted to enter his house
and to drink cold water from him,
since this one intended it
only about eating and drinking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question from Step 4 by citing a parallel משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a precise-sounding bargaining vow ('more than a סלע', 'less than a שקל') takes effect.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A parallel משנה shows that precise, extreme vow wording can still be only pressure, so it does not take effect.

steps.title: People talk this way, so the bargainers did too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the guest may drink at all, since he said 'a drop.' It answers that people talk with exaggeration like this, and the same is true of the buyer and seller.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why is he allowed? He said 'a drop of cold water'! It must be that people just talk this way. Here too, with the buyer and seller, people just talk this way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי spells out the proof. The only reason the guest may drink is that people exaggerate, so the buyer and seller were exaggerating too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question 'and why?' is not a real attack. It sharpens the point: 'a drop' sounds very exact, yet the משנה ignores it. That shows exact-sounding words in a pressure situation are just a way of talking, and the same applies to 'more than a סלע' and 'less than a שקל'.

keyTerms.meaning: And why?
Talks, speaks
A person
This way, like this

steps.confusionAlert: The question 'וְאַמַּאי' is not a challenge against רב אשי. It is part of his own proof, showing that the strong wording must be exaggeration.
steps.whatToRemember: Strong or exact-sounding words in a vow made to pressure someone can still be just exaggeration: 'משתעי איניש הכי.'

phrases.english: And why is he permitted?
But he said 'a drop of cold water'!
Rather, a person speaks this way.
Here too, a person speaks this way.
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the buyer and seller vowing on 'more than a סלע' and 'less than a שקל.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the משנה quoted in Step 5 and applies it to רבינא's case.
steps.raayaObject: The vows on 'more than a סלע' and 'less than a שקל' are only bargaining pressure and do not take effect.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה permitting the one who vowed on 'a drop of cold water' to drink, because people speak with exaggeration.

steps.title: רבינא begins his reply
steps.stepSummary: רבינא starts to answer רב אשי. His actual words come right after this.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is setting up the next move. רבינא is about to respond to רב אשי's proof, and his words come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the opening words appear here, so we don't yet know his argument. Usually this kind of reply pushes back on the comparison, showing how the two cases might be different.

phrases.english: Ravina said to him:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens רבינא's response to רב אשי's proof from the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Seems to be aimed at the comparison between the 'drop of cold water' case and the bargaining case. His actual words continue on the next amud.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not yet stated. Only the opening attribution appears here.
